description: Check a person's dietary supplements against NIH upper limits in one call. Give product names as the user said them, barcodes, NIH DSLD label IDs or custom ingredient lists; the service identifies each label in the NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database, totals every vitamin and mineral per day, and compares the totals with NIH upper limits (UL) and RDA/AI for the age and sex. It returns a plain-language agent_summary, above_ul/near_ul flags with severity, what each UL protects against, single-product changes that would bring a nutrient back under its UL, the effect of adding candidate products, and DATA_SUSPECT warnings when the NIH label record looks wrong. Also: product search (label versions collapsed), barcode lookup, normalized labels, reference values. GET /v1/tools gives JSON Schema tool definitions; GET /v1/guide a usage guide. Every number cites its label or NIH fact sheet. Label and reference data only; not medical advice; food, medications and drug interactions are not assessed (see Pocket services med-safety and fda).

rpc_types.notes: POST /v1/stack/analyze, /v1/products/search, /v1/products/lookup, /v1/products/get, /v1/nutrients/reference, /v1/tool; GET /v1/tools, /v1/guide, /v1/health, /v1/version, /openapi.json. All responses are JSON objects; errors are 4xx JSON with a stable error.code.

specs.notes: Pinned to tag v0.2.0. Also served by every backend at GET /openapi.json; tool definitions at GET /v1/tools.

serving.backend: The dietary-supplement-analysis container (Node 22) behind the HA RelayMiner with the rest backend pointed at http://<backend>:8080. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers. Needs outbound HTTPS to api.ods.od.nih.gov.
serving.notes: Optional DSLD_API_KEY. Max 15 products plus 5 candidates per analyze call; names and barcodes are resolved server-side. DSLD calls are cached (labels 7 d, searches 1 d) and capped at 8 s per request; typical response under 3 s warm. Gateway operators: type passthrough, rpc_types ["rest"], relay_timeout 30s.
